chunks: Our father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with them) narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris and Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar both narrated that Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Ali, from Abu Khalid Zayd ibn Mihran, who said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to me, from al-Husayn ibn Zayn, who said: It has reached me that Allah, the Exalted, created horses from four things: from the Great Sea that encompasses the world, and from fire, and from the tears of an angel called Ibrahim, and from a pure well. The hadith is long; we have taken from it what is needed.
ai.seo_question: What are the four things from which God created horses according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This cosmological narration from al-Khisal describes the divine creation of horses from four distinct elements: the Great Ocean, fire, the tears of the angel Ibrahim, and a pure well. It highlights the unique and mixed nature of horses in Shia theological tradition, reflecting the Ismaili and early Shia interest in elemental symbolism to explain animal characteristics. The mention of the angel Ibrahim (distinct from the Prophet Ibrahim) underscores the celestial origins attributed to these noble beasts in Islamic cosmology.
